Location: Particular Conditions material supply obligation / EOT clause / claims notice clause
Plain English Meaning: Employer-provided steel must be released in quantities and timing compatible with the accepted programme and demonstrated activity requirements.
Research the Lines: Search terms: free-issue material, reinforcement steel, delivery obligation, accepted programme, material request, shortage, critical path.
Who Holds Leverage: Contractor where readiness, requisitions, delivery records, stock balance and impacted logic are complete.
Notice / Time Bar: Issue notice when shortage becomes apparent and update particulars as deliveries and programme impacts develop.
Money Impact: Potential prolongation, disruption and idle-resource cost subject to entitlement and proof.
Schedule Impact: Potential EOT where supply shortage affects the critical or longest path.
Practical Action / Evidence: Material requisitions, delivery notes, stock ledger, bar schedules, daily reports, photographs, P6 updates and TIA fragnet.

Clause / Topic: Revised IFC structural and embedded-service details
Location: Design information clause / delayed drawings clause / EOT and claims provisions
Plain English Meaning: Late or conflicting design information may excuse delay when the affected work cannot reasonably proceed without an approved resolution.
Research the Lines: Search terms: revised IFC, design conflict, embedded sleeves, waterstop, opening detail, hold point, approval.
Who Holds Leverage: Contractor when submissions were timely and the unresolved issue controlled execution.
Notice / Time Bar: Notify on discovery and issue an updated notice after final revised drawings are received.
Money Impact: May support prolongation or disruption cost where compensability and causation are demonstrated.
Schedule Impact: Supports EOT where engineering release drives a critical construction activity.
Practical Action / Evidence: RFI register, drawing transmittals, review comments, revised IFCs, technical meeting minutes and schedule linkage.

Location: Engineer response period / cooperation duty / EOT and claim provisions
Plain English Meaning: A delayed response can be a compensable event where the requested clarification was necessary and the contractor had no reasonable alternative.
Research the Lines: Search terms: RFI, response due date, technical clarification, inspection hold, approved detail.
Who Holds Leverage: Contractor if the RFI is specific, timely and linked to a ready activity.
Notice / Time Bar: Notify after the contractual response period expires and maintain updated particulars.
Money Impact: Potential prolongation and disruption subject to concurrency and mitigation analysis.
Schedule Impact: Supports EOT only where the response delay controls critical work.
Practical Action / Evidence: RFI issue/reply dates, correspondence, readiness evidence, manpower records and impacted programme.

Location: Interim payment clause / delayed payment interest / suspension and claims provisions
Plain English Meaning: Late certification or payment may create financing and resource constraints, but time and cost consequences require separate causal proof.
Research the Lines: Search terms: interim payment, certification period, cheque receipt, interest, financing cost, resource reduction.
Who Holds Leverage: Shared; contractor must establish both contractual default and actual causal impact.
Notice / Time Bar: Submit payment default notice, interest calculation and updated impact records.
Money Impact: Interest and financing cost may be recoverable where contractually allowed.
Schedule Impact: Usually secondary unless procurement or resources on the critical path were directly affected.
Practical Action / Evidence: Invoices, certificates, bank receipts, cash-flow statements, purchase orders and recovery records.
